findings: The clone is NOT placeholder-only: the home components and src/data/pages-content.json hold the studio's real brand name, address, phone, email, team names, client and project names, award and press names, testimonials and 10 full blog posts, and public/ ships the real client logos, project images, team portraits, fonts and Lottie JSON. CLONE_SPEC.md says copy and logos are not reproduced; CLONE_SPEC-PAGES.md says the owner clones their own site with real content. This design-repo therefore treats the clone itself as sensitive source (docs/sensitivity-and-licensing.md) and hashes names and copy in schema/protected-content.json.

ia/ia.json (9 templates, 34 sections, 18 routes) was spot-checked against src/Router.jsx and the DOM: every route and section id reconciles. The design-repo decomposes ia content.blog-body into per-chapter sections and the 25-card /work grid and 10-card /blog grid into clusters (see each contract's measured.decomposition); several ia sections share one contract via iaSectionIds.

Measured at 1440: tallest HERO hero.article-header 850px; largest in-flow share 41% (conversion.enquiry-form on /contact), reported by extraction/wrapper_gate.py. Without decomposition /work (86% in one grid) and /blog (83%) would exceed the 60% gate.

src/pages/pages.css and CLONE_SPEC-PAGES.md note one image missing locally (team member 12); the home Work section and the live site randomise the 3 home blog cards (Webflow shuffle): the clone shows the cached trio.

The clone has no prefers-reduced-motion handling; motion is gated by breakpoint (<=767 static). Reduced-motion fallbacks in motion-patterns.json are what generated pages must do, not what the clone does.
Visual parity against the live site was NOT measured in this build (no live-vs-clone pixel harness was run); no percentage is claimed.

parity.note: No live-vs-clone pixel harness was run for this design-repo, so no parity number exists. The clone's own QA evidence is in CLONE_SPEC*.md and its commit history.
